title: Launch Video Setup
bottom_line: Run the setup command once inside your app's repo. Claude checks the tools the launch videos need and installs what is missing, step by step.

sections.heading: Run it once, inside your app's repo

blocks.text: In Claude Code, open your app's repo and type the command below. You only need it the first time. It takes no arguments.

blocks.caption: First time only: checks and installs tools.

blocks.title: What it does for you and what it asks of you

cards.title: Claude does
cards.text: Everything a command can do: installing packages, editing PATH, creating the emulator, writing the key file.

cards.title: You do
cards.text: Only what needs a human: creating an account, clicking through an installer, approving a password prompt.

blocks.text: The setup skill prepares your computer so the other launch-video skills can run, and it is written for people who may be non-technical. It finds what is missing and fixes it.

blocks.title: When to use it
blocks.text: Use it when you are setting up, installing or preparing for the launch video, when one of the launch-video skills reports something MISSING, when you ask "what do I need" for the video, or when a launch-video script fails because a tool is not found.

blocks.title: What it can check and install
items: ffmpeg, the program that stitches video clips together, built with libass for captions
An ElevenLabs key for the voice-over (a free ElevenLabs account)
For Android apps: Java, the Android command-line tools and emulator (or a real phone), and Maestro
For web apps: the Playwright package and Chromium

blocks.text: The README also lists a free HeyGen or Synthesia account for the presenter clips. That part is manual and guided.

sections.heading: You are only ever asked to do one thing at a time

blocks.title: One message, one action
blocks.caption: Claude never takes "done" on faith. If the step did not work, it says what it saw in one sentence and gives the next single thing to try.

blocks.title: What that means in practice
items: Each message ends with exactly one action for you, in plain language, followed by "Tell me when that's done".
Even if three things are missing, they are handled one at a time.
Jargon comes with a one-phrase explanation, for example "ffmpeg (the program that stitches video clips together)".

sections.heading: The setup runs in four steps

steps.title: Find out what you are making
steps.text: If the conversation or the repo does not make it clear, Claude asks one question: "Is your launch video for a phone app (Android) or for a web app?" An `AndroidManifest.xml` or `build.gradle` means Android app; a FastAPI, Django or Next.js project means web app.

steps.title: Run the checker
steps.text: The checker prints an OK/MISSING table for app, webapp or both. Claude tells you briefly what is already fine and how many things are missing, for example "Three things need installing; let's go one at a time.", then goes straight to the first missing item.

steps.title: Fix missing items one at a time
steps.text: If a command can install it, Claude runs it and tells you in one sentence, such as "Installing ffmpeg now, this takes a minute." An admin password prompt is then your one action. Sign-ups, installers or plugging in a phone get a single next action. Claude re-runs the checker before moving on.

steps.title: Confirm and hand over
steps.text: When the checker prints "everything is set up", Claude tells you that you are ready and that the next thing to do is run `/launch-video:launch-video-app` or `/launch-video:launch-video-webapp`.

blocks.title: Order for Android
blocks.text: For an Android app the order matters: Java, then the Android tools, then Maestro. The virtual device is created after the emulator exists.

sections.heading: The checker looks for these items

rows: 3.9 or newer, for the helper scripts
Needed by Android tools and Maestro
Android emulator (or connect a real phone with USB debugging)
Installed with `python3 -m pip install playwright` and `python3 -m playwright install chromium`

sections.heading: Your ElevenLabs key is stored in your home folder

steps.title: Create a free account
steps.text: Claude walks you through creating a free account at elevenlabs.io.

steps.title: Create a key
steps.text: Go to Profile → API Keys → Create.

steps.title: Paste it into the chat
steps.text: Claude writes it to `~/.launch-video/env` as `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=<key>`, creates the folder, runs `chmod 600` on the file, and confirms with the checker. It never echoes the key back in full afterwards.

blocks.text: The key is read from the `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` environment variable, or from the file `~/.launch-video/env`.

All configuration lives in `~/.launch-video/`, never inside the plugin's own folder. A plugin update replaces that folder, and your home folder is the only place that survives an update. The plugin turns an app repo into a launch/promo video: AI presenter intro/outro, real screen recordings, voice-over, and captions. It has no plugin settings, no dependencies and no userConfig.

sections.heading: Common snags have a known fix

cards.title: Emulator install is painful
cards.text: A real Android phone works instead and skips the emulator and virtual device steps. If you have one handy and the emulator install is painful, Claude offers it.

points.text: Claude offers one action: enable USB debugging and plug it in.

cards.title: You are on Windows
cards.text: The scripts are bash and run on macOS and Linux. Git Bash is not enough for the Android emulator.

points.text: Use WSL (Ubuntu) and run everything inside it.

cards.title: Installed but not on PATH
cards.text: The checker says so, and Claude adds a line to your shell profile.

points.text: Open a new terminal window and run the setup command again.

cards.title: Captions (libass) missing
cards.text: On macOS, Homebrew's plain `ffmpeg` is built without libass, so captions cannot work.

points.text: Claude reinstalls a libass-enabled ffmpeg itself, with no admin password.

blocks.title: Windows details
blocks.text: If the checker reports "Windows (Git Bash)", the first single action is installing WSL.

blocks.title: PATH details
blocks.text: The shell profile is `~/.zshrc` on macOS and `~/.bashrc` on Linux or WSL.

blocks.title: The captions fix
blocks.text: This is a same-for-same reinstall, not data loss. Claude runs this command:

blocks.code: brew uninstall ffmpeg && brew tap homebrew-ffmpeg/ffmpeg && brew install homebrew-ffmpeg/ffmpeg/ffmpeg

sections.heading: Done means the checker says everything is set up

before.label: Before
before.text: The checker shows one or more MISSING lines, and the launch-video skills report something MISSING.

after.label: After
after.text: The checker prints "everything is set up", and Claude points you to `/launch-video:launch-video-app` or `/launch-video:launch-video-webapp`.

blocks.title: Coming back later
blocks.text: If you come back later, Claude just runs the checker again, because it is the source of truth. It does not ask what you did last time.

next_action.text: Open your app's repo in Claude Code and run `/launch-video:launch-video-setup`.
next_action.detail: It is only needed the first time, and Claude asks you for one thing at a time.
